Esbjerg: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic in Esbjerg) is a psychiatric department within Region Syddanmark (Region of Southern Denmark) that is actively monitored in the national tracking of ADHD diagnostic practices. The clinic's performance is specifically evaluated against [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], a clinical quality metric that measures the proportion of ADHD diagnostic processes for children aged 0–5 years in which the child receives a clinical environmental observation within 120 days of the assessment's initiation [^src2]. 

During the 2023/24 reporting period, the Esbjerg clinic recorded a 78% fulfillment rate for [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], successfully completing the required observations for 18 out of 23 eligible cases [^src1]. Because the national standard demands a fulfillment rate of ≥ 90%, the department officially did not meet the standard for this indicator [^src1]. The clinic's results contribute to a broader regional decline in target fulfillment across Region Syddanmark, a trend that annual reports suggest is likely driven by a shortage of medical staff and systemic resource allocation challenges [^src2]. While certain clinics in the region, such as those in Vejle and Aabenraa, manage to consistently meet or approach the 90% development goal, the Esbjerg department's data underscores the capacity constraints and geographical variations in clinical practice currently affecting Danish child and adolescent psychiatry [^src2].
